region.name: Jezero Crater
region.why: Mars 2020 Perseverance landing region: an ancient crater lake with a preserved delta, giving a clear exploration-and-science narrative and a well-documented start point.

processing_steps.note: Clipped to whole source pixels; values unchanged.
shot-count grid verified identical to topography grid (same ppd, origin, shape)
slope = atan(|grad z|) by central differences with dx = dy*cos(lat); relief = 3x3 max-min; hillshade az 315°, alt 45°, 3x vertical exaggeration (display only)

routing grid 1/512° and analysis grid 1/1024°: cubic-spline interpolation (scipy.ndimage.map_coordinates, order=3, prefilter=True; edges padded 8 cells by odd reflection) of the native 1/128° grid; shot counts by nearest neighbour. Built at start-up from grid.npz; finer spacing does not add terrain information.

Bins with zero MOLA shots are interpolated (label: up to 12 km between profiles)
Heights are relative to the MOLA areoid

targets.name: Octavia E. Butler Landing (Perseverance landing site)
targets.source: NASA named the Mars 2020 landing site on 5 March 2021; published coordinates 18.4447°N, 77.4508°E (≈18°26'N 77°27'E). Cited value — no local source file, not re-checked in the offline build, so it is not marked VERIFIED.
targets.why: Documented, real starting point on the crater floor.
targets.limitation: Position precision ~0.01°; one MOLA cell is ~0.008°.
targets.fixture_note: Shown on SYNTHETIC terrain — terrain values near this point are not real.

targets.name: Jezero crater (centre)
targets.source: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature value (18.38°N, 77.58°E). Cited value — no local source file, not re-checked in the offline build, so it is not marked VERIFIED.
targets.why: Reference point used to locate the crater rim.
targets.limitation: Nomenclature centre, not a surveyed point.
targets.fixture_note: Shown on SYNTHETIC terrain — terrain values near this point are not real.

targets.name: Western delta front
targets.source: NASA describes the fan-shaped sedimentary deposit (delta) west of the landing site; position here is an approximate placement from published maps.
targets.why: Deltas form where a river entered a lake; their layered sediments can record past water and environments.
targets.investigate: Layering, grain size and composition of sedimentary rocks exposed at the front.
targets.limitation: APPROXIMATE position — verify against the real MOLA hillshade / HiRISE before presenting. Composition is not measured by MOLA.
targets.offline_review: Not refined in the offline v2 build (2026-10-10): the only local terrain is the SYNTHETIC fixture, which carries no evidence about the real delta. The fan-shaped bump in the fixture is generated by scripts/make_fixture.py and must not be used to move this point. Check it in QGIS with real CTX/MOLA data (docs/DATA.md).
targets.fixture_note: Shown on SYNTHETIC terrain — terrain values near this point are not real.

targets.name: Jezero west rim crest (derived)
targets.source: Highest synthetic-fixture elevation (-2196 m) sampled along the azimuth from the crater centre through the landing site, between 0.70 and 1.35 crater radii (found at 1.00 R).
targets.why: Impact-crater rims expose material uplifted from depth; a rim position also gives the crew a regional overview.
targets.investigate: Rim-forming rock types and their relation to crater-floor and delta deposits.
targets.limitation: Located on SYNTHETIC terrain: this point is a pipeline demonstration, not the real rim crest. Located from ~463 m topography only; the exact crest and access path need HiRISE-scale data.
targets.fixture_note: Shown on SYNTHETIC terrain — terrain values near this point are not real.

grid_records.product: elevation resampled to 1/512° for route search
grid_records.spatial_reference: Simple cylindrical lat/lon grid, same outer bounds as the native clipped grid
processing_steps: cubic-spline interpolation (scipy.ndimage.map_coordinates, order=3, prefilter=True; edges padded 8 cells by odd reflection) of the native 1/128° grid; shot counts by nearest neighbour
grid_records.notes: finer spacing does NOT add terrain information; the effective resolution is still the native grid
limitations: Interpolation does not add real terrain detail; effective resolution stays ~463 m
Cubic splines can overshoot near sharp breaks, so fine-grid maximum slopes can exceed native ones
Slope limit (exclusion) is an ASSUMPTION applied unchanged at every grid spacing
